beginner.summary: For Python developers who have called an LLM API and now want to build agents and small teams with AutoGen 0.4 and later (the layered autogen-agentchat, autogen-core and autogen-ext packages). Covers where AutoGen stands today next to Microsoft Agent Framework, installing and pinning packages, model clients, AssistantAgent, messages and TaskResult, streaming, function tools, termination conditions, RoundRobinGroupChat, human input, state, model context, structured output, local models, memory, code execution, AutoGen Studio, logging and a research-team capstone.
prerequisites: Writes Python 3.10+ with async/await and can use virtual environments and pip
Has an API key for an OpenAI-compatible or Azure OpenAI model, or can run Ollama locally
Has used a chat-completions API and understands prompts, tokens and JSON
outcomes: Install AutoGen 0.4+ packages, pin versions and run agents against hosted and local models
Build AssistantAgent instances with function tools, structured output, memory and model context limits
Compose agents into RoundRobinGroupChat teams with termination conditions and human input
Deliver a tested research-team application with logs, saved state and a documented upgrade path to Microsoft Agent Framework

intermediate.summary: For developers who can already build single agents and RoundRobinGroupChat teams in AutoGen and now need dynamic orchestration. Covers SelectorGroupChat with custom selector and candidate functions, Swarm and handoffs, GraphFlow with DiGraphBuilder, MagenticOneGroupChat and web or file agents, MCP tools through McpWorkbench, AgentTool and TeamTool, custom BaseChatAgent classes, vector memory, token-limited context, declarative configuration, cancellation, Docker code executors, multi-provider clients, replay-based testing, OpenTelemetry tracing and a swarm-based support capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the beginner AutoGen course or builds AssistantAgent tools and RoundRobinGroupChat teams with termination conditions
Reads async Python and writes pytest tests
Has Docker, Node.js (for MCP servers) and an LLM API key or a local Ollama model available
outcomes: Choose between selector, swarm, graph and Magentic-One orchestration for a given workflow
Connect agents to MCP servers, other agents and vector memory while controlling context size
Persist, serialise and test teams with state files, declarative JSON and a replay model client
Trace and cancel multi-agent runs and deliver a swarm-based support application

advanced.summary: For engineers who run AutoGen teams and now need to design on autogen-core, operate multi-agent services and plan the move to Microsoft Agent Framework. Covers the Core runtime, RoutedAgent handlers, topics and subscriptions, direct RPC messaging, lifecycle and state, hand-written tool loops, intervention handlers, gRPC distributed workers, message serialisation, Core design patterns, custom model clients and caching, the component system, FastAPI streaming, agent security, cost control, evaluation, reliability, production telemetry, migration to Microsoft Agent Framework and a distributed capstone.
prerequisites: Has completed the intermediate AutoGen course or has built SelectorGroupChat, Swarm and tool-using teams with tests
Understands asyncio tasks, queues, Pydantic models and Docker networking
Can run a gRPC service, a FastAPI app and an OpenTelemetry collector locally
outcomes: Design event-driven agent systems on autogen-core with topics, RPC calls, interventions and distributed workers
Harden agent services with sandboxing, tool allow-lists, budgets, retries, evaluation and production telemetry
Extend AutoGen with custom model clients, caching and components
Produce a migration plan from AutoGen to Microsoft Agent Framework backed by tests and a working distributed service
